minimum_answer: Failing input: a=[1,2], t=2. Initially l=0, r=1, m=0; a[0]=1<2 so l=m=0, and l<r still holds, so the loop never makes progress and returns 0, but the correct answer is 1. Repair using a half-open interval: l=0, r=len(a); while l<r: m=(l+r)//2; if a[m]<t: l=m+1 else: r=m; return l. Termination: each iteration either sets l=m+1>l or r=m<r, so r-l strictly decreases and the loop ends. Correctness: maintain that all indices <l have a[i]<t and all indices >=r have a[i]>=t; when a[m]<t, indices <=m are below t so l=m+1 is safe; otherwise a[m]>=t so r=m is safe. At exit l=r, so l is the smallest index with a[l]>=t, or len(a) if none exists. Duplicates are handled because the else branch moves r left past equal values; t above all entries drives l to len(a).
